nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer days power the tussac, shrubs, kelp and plankton that the whole web is built on.

nodes.name: Cold, nutrient-rich current
nodes.desc: Cold water of the Falkland Current flows north along the Patagonian Shelf and carries nutrients that feed plankton and kelp.

nodes.name: Wet coastal ground
nodes.desc: Tussac forms dense stands on wet ground close to the shore, and dead plant matter and seabird waste are recycled there.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, kelp, carcasses and droppings, returning nutrients to the soil and water.

nodes.name: Tussac grass
nodes.desc: A tall coastal grass that grows in dense clumps about 2 m high and dominates the shoreline where it grows. Penguins, albatrosses and seals use it for cover and nesting.

nodes.name: Diddle-dee
nodes.desc: A low dwarf shrub of the treeless Falklands heath. It bears berries and was among the most recorded plants near this site.

nodes.name: Giant kelp
nodes.desc: Large brown seaweed forming kelp beds in the cold coastal water around the islands.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae in the surrounding sea, the base of the open-water food chain.

nodes.name: Lobster krill
nodes.desc: A small red squat lobster that swarms in the waters around the Falklands and southern South America and feeds many seabirds and fish.

nodes.name: Kelp goose
nodes.desc: A shoreline goose of southern South America that grazes seaweed on rocky coasts. It was one of the most recorded birds here.

nodes.name: Sheep
nodes.desc: Introduced livestock; virtually all land on the islands is used as sheep pasture, where they graze native grasses.

nodes.name: Austral thrush
nodes.desc: A common songbird that nests in tussac on the Falklands. It feeds on invertebrates and berries.

nodes.name: Patagonian squid
nodes.desc: A small squid fished in Falklands waters and an important prey for seabirds, seals and fish.

nodes.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
nodes.desc: Breeds in colonies on the Falklands and eats mainly krill and other crustaceans, plus squid and some fish.

nodes.name: Magellanic penguin
nodes.desc: A burrowing penguin breeding on the islands and one of the most recorded birds near this site. It eats fish, squid and crustaceans.

nodes.name: Black-browed albatross
nodes.desc: The Falklands hold the largest breeding population in the world. It eats fish, squid, crustaceans, carrion and fishery discards.

nodes.name: Southern elephant seal
nodes.desc: Breeds on Falkland beaches; a large seal that dives for squid and fish.

nodes.name: Brown skua
nodes.desc: A bold seabird that takes eggs and chicks from penguin colonies and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Southern giant petrel
nodes.desc: A large scavenging seabird that feeds on carrion from seals and penguins and also preys on penguin chicks.

nodes.name: Striated caracara
nodes.desc: A rare raptor of offshore islands. It scavenges and also takes seabird eggs and chicks, penguins and seal pups.

nodes.name: South American sea lion
nodes.desc: Eats fish, squid and crustaceans and also hunts penguins. The Falklands population is declining.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: Seen around the Falklands and recorded hunting seals and sea lions.
